Single-letter flags with a non-ASCII name (e.g. Hebrew or Cyrillic) are not recognized

With urfave/cli v3, a flag whose name is a single non-ASCII letter cannot be used on the command line, and it is shown with the wrong prefix in help/docs.

Minimal reproduction:

```go
cmd := &cli.Command{
    Name:  "app",
    Flags: []cli.Flag{&cli.StringFlag{Name: "ש"}},
    Action: func(_ context.Context, cmd *cli.Command) error {
        fmt.Printf("value=%q args=%q\n", cmd.String("ש"), cmd.Args().Slice())
        return nil
    },
}
cmd.Run(context.Background(), []string{"app", "-ש", "value", "operand"})
```

Actual: the flag is not parsed at all; `-ש`, `value` and `operand` are all treated as positional arguments and `cmd.String("ש")` is empty.
Expected: `value="value" args=["operand"]`, exactly like an ASCII single-letter flag such as `-s value operand`.

Also, help output and generated docs render this flag as `--ש`; like any other one-letter flag name it should be rendered with a single dash, `-ש`. ASCII flags and multi-letter flags must keep working as they do today.
